## Effect-size definition

This task uses the equal-variance, independent-groups pooled-standard-deviation definition. The standard deviation within each group is a sample standard deviation, so the variance denominator is \(n-1\).

\[
s_p=
\sqrt{
\frac{(n_{\mathrm{KD}}-1)s_{\mathrm{KD}}^2+
(n_{\mathrm{CTRL}}-1)s_{\mathrm{CTRL}}^2}
{n_{\mathrm{KD}}+n_{\mathrm{CTRL}}-2}
}
\]

\[
d=
\frac{\overline{x}_{\mathrm{KD}}-\overline{x}_{\mathrm{CTRL}}}
{s_p}
\]

The numerator direction is fixed as `KD - CTRL`. Although the original records are paired by Sample, the standard deviation of the paired differences is not used here.

# Reduced NeuN abundance in knockdown hemispheres quantified by a pooled effect size

Bianca L. Shore, Farid M. Rahimi, Haruto Endo, and Janice P. Cole

## Abstract

Standardised effect sizes facilitate comparison of neuronal knockdown phenotypes across experiments with different count dispersion. We measured NeuN-positive nuclei in eight knockdown and eight control hemispheres and estimated Cohen's \(d\) with the independent-groups pooled standard deviation. With the contrast oriented as knockdown minus control, NeuN abundance was lower in the knockdown condition, producing **\(d=-0.48\)**. Heteroscedasticity-robust sensitivity analysis yielded the same direction and a comparable magnitude. The result indicates a moderate reduction in neuronal nuclei counts following knockdown.
